title: Sum Object Values
description: Given an object where all values are numbers, return the sum of all values.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize a total to 0.
Use Object.values() to get an array of the values.
Loop through the values and add each to the total.
Return the total.
patternExplanation: Object.values() converts an object's values into a plain array — you can then use any array loop pattern on them without needing for...in.

title: Invert an Object
description: Given an object, return a new object where the keys and values are swapped. Assume all values are unique strings or numbers.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result object.
Use Object.entries() to get [key, value] pairs.
For each pair, assign result[value] = key.
Return the result object.
patternExplanation: Object.entries() yields [key, value] tuples — destructuring them in the loop header makes swapping or transforming key-value pairs clean and direct.

title: Deep Equal Comparison
description: Write a function that deeply compares two objects or values for equality, checking all keys and nested structures recursively.
whatShouldHappen: If values are strictly identical (===), return true.
If either is null, or not an object, return false.
Check array matching: if Array.isArray differs, return false.
Verify Object.keys lengths are equal.
Recursively compare every key's corresponding value.
patternExplanation: Traversing keys recursively handles nested object hierarchies while properly short-circuiting on primitive mismatches.

title: Invert Object Keys and Values
description: Given an object, return a new object where keys become values and values become keys. If multiple keys have the same value, group the original keys into an array.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result object.
Loop through each key in the input object using for...in with hasOwnProperty.
Convert value to string for inverted key.
If the new key already exists, convert to or push into an array.
Otherwise, assign the single key as value.
patternExplanation: Flipping keys and values tests dynamic key access and handling collisions through conditional array accumulation.

title: Pick Object Properties
description: Given an object and an array of string keys, return a new object containing only the properties whose keys appear in the provided keys array.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize picked object = {}.
Create a Set from the keys array for fast O(1) checks.
Iterate over keys in Set: if obj has property, copy it to picked.
Return the picked object.
patternExplanation: Filtering object properties based on a whitelist is a core utility pattern in data sanitization and state manipulation.

title: Count Frequency of Elements
description: Given an array of string items, return an object mapping each unique item to its count of occurrences in the array.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty object freq = {}.
Loop through each item in the items array.
Set freq[item] = (freq[item] || 0) + 1.
Return freq.
patternExplanation: Using an object as a hash map to aggregate item counts in a single O(n) pass is the basis of countless frequency patterns.
